To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a method to compute path travel time distributions on a large road network using GPS traces, that we develop a ‘stop-and-go’ algorithm to compress the raw GPS traces, and that we develop scalable inference algorithms for computing the distributions.
we propose a method to accurately estimate travel time distributions for large-scale road networks using GPS probe vehicle data.

(1) we developed a scalable algorithm for estimating travel time distributions for large road networks, using a composite Markov model and Gaussian Markov Random Field, (2) the algorithm scales linearly in the number of road links in the network, (3) the method is accurate, with a mean absolute error of 0.8 minutes, and a standard deviation of 2 minutes.
